front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《24》

en: This summer, I will not travel far
Right there in Liao Chi-chun's painting
Look, the shadow of the banana tree

points.zh:
廖繼春，1902 年出生於豐原農家，自幼家境清苦。師範學校畢業後，在未婚妻資助下，於 1924 年赴東京美術學校深造。1928 年以作品《芭蕉之庭》入選帝展。回台後以教職終生，桃李滿天下。廖繼春是台灣前輩畫家中，極富眾望與親和力的一位。他在繪畫方面的成就輝煌，擅於掌控色彩，濃重的彩度及明快的節奏是他作品的特色之一，畫作明朗有深度，歡悅中見抒情。他不僅在戰前，即擁有可觀的繪畫資歷與創作成就，到了戰後，也同樣以常春的創作活力，贏得了新生代的敬重。雖然廖繼春一生曾經歷烽火歲月與憂患貧苦，但他的彩筆卻揮灑一片令人嚮往的抒情世界。他的藝術，如同一道七色耀眼的彩虹，超然而壯麗的跨越了新舊時代之間的鴻溝，昂然從戰前的過去闊步到戰後的現代。( 資料取自文建會《台灣網路美術舘》網站 )
廖繼春 ( 1902 ~ 1976 ) 在1927年以兩幅作品入選首屆臺灣美術展覽會（臺展），第二年以「有香蕉樹的院子」這幅畫，入選日本第九屆帝國美術院展覽會（帝展），受到畫壇的重視與肯定，這是廖繼春的成名之作。畫中最入目的，是直立在前景的香蕉樹，拔挺、繁盛、充滿活力。厝角鄉婦的作息，則在陽光直射、折射、反射的光影變化中，襯托出南台灣夏天的迷離氛圍。斑駁的樹影，交錯投射在斜向的地面和外牆，刻劃出空間的深度感。廖繼春用層次十分豐富的色調，描繪出陽光穿梭在物象之間，所帶來的光影對照的變化。在炎熱的夏天，香蕉樹益發翠綠，與熾烈的陽光形成對比，而蔭影籠罩的紅色暈染，亦與遠處向陽白牆對應出色澤的節奏。此畫不僅顯示流暢與敏感的畫作技巧，也映照出南台灣的自然氣息和人文抒情。畫裡所呈現的色調，強烈卻又和諧，這種畫風一直持續在他往後的作品。
points.en:
Liao Chi-chun was born in 1902 into a farming family in Fengyuan, and had a poor and difficult childhood. After graduating from normal school, he traveled to Tokyo School of Fine Arts in 1924 to further his studies, funded by his fiancée. In 1928, his work 'Courtyard with Banana Trees' was selected for the Imperial Exhibition. After returning to Taiwan he spent his career teaching, with students filling the land. Liao Chi-chun was one of the most respected and approachable senior painters of Taiwan. His achievements in painting were brilliant; skilled at handling color, rich saturation and lively rhythm are among the hallmarks of his work, his paintings bright yet full of depth, joyful yet lyrical. Even before the war he already had considerable painting experience and achievement, and after the war he won the respect of the new generation with the same evergreen creative vitality. Although Liao Chi-chun's life passed through years of war and hardship and poverty, his brush painted a lyrical world that people long for. His art, like a dazzling seven-colored rainbow, transcended and magnificently bridged the gap between the old and new eras, striding boldly from the prewar past into the postwar present. (Material drawn from the Council for Cultural Affairs' "Taiwan Online Art Museum" website.)
Liao Chi-chun (1902–1976) had two works selected for the first Taiwan Fine Arts Exhibition (Taiten) in 1927, and the following year his painting "Courtyard with Banana Trees" was selected for the ninth Imperial Art Academy Exhibition (Teiten) in Japan, earning him recognition and acclaim in the art world — this became Liao's breakthrough work. The most eye-catching element of the painting is the banana tree standing upright in the foreground, tall, lush, and full of vitality. The daily life of village women at the corner of a house is set amid the shifting play of direct, refracted, and reflected sunlight, evoking the hazy atmosphere of a southern Taiwan summer. The dappled shadows of the trees, cast crosswise on the slanted ground and outer wall, carve out a sense of spatial depth. Liao used richly layered tones to depict how sunlight weaves among objects, bringing changing contrasts of light and shadow. In the hot summer, the banana trees appear ever more emerald green, contrasting with the fierce sunlight, while the reddish glow beneath the shade corresponds in rhythm to the sunlit white wall in the distance. This painting displays not only fluent and sensitive technique but also reflects the natural atmosphere and human warmth of southern Taiwan. The tones in the painting are strong yet harmonious, a style that persisted throughout his later works.

en: A long, long road
Arriving beneath the flowering tree
Only wish to watch the sunset with you
The footsteps of the years
Light as mist
A silent urging
Setting sun, drifting clouds
The wild ferry crossing, no one about
How much wind and rain does it take to call it parting sorrow?

points.zh:
青山橫北郭，白水繞東城。
此地一為別，孤蓬萬里征。
浮雲遊子意，落日故人情。
揮手自茲去，蕭蕭班馬鳴。
--唐。 李白《 送友人 》
points.en:
Green mountains lie across the northern wall; white water winds round the eastern city.
Here we part once, and you drift ten thousand miles like a lone tumbleweed.
Floating clouds — the wanderer's mood; the setting sun — an old friend's feeling.
We wave and part from here, as our horses neigh, parting from each other.
-- Tang Dynasty. Li Bai, "Seeing Off a Friend"

en: Old temple, broken pillars, scattered and uneven
Everything has been lost
Nothing at all has been lost
Dusk, a white egret
Looking back again and again
The lonely homeward road of the water buffalo
The stone splits, the sky startles, waking
The old dream of the Red Chamber
In the dream, I did not know I was a guest

points.zh:
曹雪芹的《紅樓夢》又名《石頭記》
「 簾外雨潺潺，春意闌珊，羅衾不耐五更寒。夢裡不知身是客，一响貪歡。獨自莫憑樓，無限江山，別時容易見時難。流水落花春去也，天上人間。」 --李後主《 浪淘沙 》
points.en:
Cao Xueqin's 'Dream of the Red Chamber,' also known as 'The Story of the Stone'
"Outside the curtain the rain patters on, spring's glory is fading; the silk quilt cannot keep out the chill of the fifth watch. In my dream I did not know myself a guest, greedily seeking pleasure for one brief moment. Alone, do not lean upon the balcony rail, for boundless rivers and mountains lie beyond — parting was easy, but meeting again is hard. The flowing water, the fallen blossoms, spring has gone away — as different as heaven from the human world." -- Li Houzhu, 'Waves Scouring the Sand'

en: Like the evening sun, like the morning dew
Like a faint rain in the forest
Metaphors -- there's no time even for metaphors
A winding lane, cold rain
A fallen leaf
The music, lyrical as ever
Take that stretch of blue
Give it back to the beach, captain
And, grandmother's Penghu Bay

points.zh:
詞 / 曲 :  葉佳修《外婆的澎湖灣 》歌詞:
晚風輕拂着澎湖灣， 白浪逐沙灘。 没有椰林醉斜陽，只是一片海藍藍。坐在門前的矮牆上，一遍遍回想，也是黄昏的沙灘上，有着脚印两對半。那是外婆拄着杖，將我手輕輕挽， 踩着薄暮走向餘暉，暖暖的澎湖灣， 一个脚印是笑語一串，消磨許多時光，直到夜色吞没我俩，在回家的路上。澎湖灣啊，澎湖湾，外婆的澎湖灣，有我许多的童年幻想，陽光，沙灘，海浪，仙人掌，還有一位老船長。
阳光天使 - 外婆的澎湖湾 [Official Music Video]
台灣原聲童聲合唱團2016休士頓巡演下半場 外婆的澎湖灣
points.en:
Lyrics/Music: Yeh Chia-hsiu, "Grandma's Penghu Bay" — lyrics:
The evening breeze gently caresses Penghu Bay, white waves chase along the sand. There's no coconut grove drunk in the slanting sun, only a stretch of deep blue sea. Sitting on the low wall in front of the door, recalling it again and again — it was also on a dusk-lit beach that there were two and a half sets of footprints. That was Grandma leaning on her cane, gently taking my hand, treading through the fading light toward the glow of dusk, the warm Penghu Bay — each footprint a string of laughter, whiling away so much time, until the night swallowed us both, on the way home. Penghu Bay, oh, Penghu Bay, Grandma's Penghu Bay, holds so many of my childhood fantasies — sunshine, sandy beach, ocean waves, cactus, and an old sea captain.
"Sunshine Angels — Grandma's Penghu Bay" [Official Music Video]
Taiwan Voices Children's Choir 2016 Houston Tour, Second Half: "Grandma's Penghu Bay"
